assays.assay_description: Standard EPM with two open and two closed arms (30 x 5 cm) elevated 40 cm; single 5 min test session per mouse. Measures: % entries and % time in open arms, entries into closed arms, and risk-assessment time.

application_type.evidence: Ayahuasca was administered orally at a dose of 1.5 mL/kg

setup_restrain.evidence: Each mouse was placed in the center section and left to explore the maze

food_restriction.evidence: no food in test apparatus; home-cage food ad libitum

time_to_assay.evidence: One day after the last ayahuasca exposure, the mice were subjected to the Morris water maze (MWM), open field and elevated plus maze tasks

outcomes.summary: Ayahuasca did not change open-arm entries or time across any age group, but increased risk-assessment behavior in mice exposed during childhood; this effect did not persist into later groups.
outcomes.statistics: risk assessment childhood [t(19)=-3.2684; P=0.0040]; other groups non-significant; open-arm entries and time non-significant across all groups
outcomes.evidence: Mice treated with ayahuasca in childhood spent more time in risk assessment than control mice [t(19)=-3.2684; P=0.0040]

assays.assay_description: Circular water pool (150 cm diameter, 8 cm deep) with submerged hidden platform. Acquisition: 4 trials/day for 5 consecutive days (D2-D6), max 120 s/trial. Probe trial: 60 s free swim on D7 with platform removed. Measures: latency to platform, time in platform quadrant, distance in quadrant, platform-zone crossings.

application_type.evidence: Ayahuasca was administered orally at a dose of 1.5 mL/kg

setup_restrain.evidence: mouse was lowered into the water by its tail and allowed to swim freely

food_restriction.evidence: no food in test apparatus; home-cage food ad libitum

water_restriction.evidence: pool containing 8 cm deep water (test medium)

time_to_assay.evidence: One day after the last ayahuasca exposure, the mice were subjected to the Morris water maze

outcomes.summary: All groups acquired the spatial task. During the probe trial, adolescent ayahuasca-treated mice spent less time in the platform quadrant and crossed it fewer times than controls, suggesting spatial memory impairment. Acquisition latency showed treatment × time interactions in childhood, childhood-adolescence, and adolescent-adult groups.
outcomes.statistics: Probe adolescence: time in quadrant t(20)=-2.6937, P=0.0139; crossings t(20)=-2.3350, P=0.0300. Acquisition (ANOVA): Adol treatment effect F(1,20)=7.1250, P=0.0147; Adol-Adult F(1,17)=4.5188, P=0.0485; significant time x treatment interactions for Child [F(4,76)=2.5764, P=0.0441], Child-Adol [F(4,60)=6.1132, P=0.0012], and Adol-Adult [F(4,68)=3.2988, P=0.0157].
outcomes.evidence: Student's t-test detected a significant effect of treatment in adolescence, with mice that received ayahuasca spending less time in the platform quadrant than the control group [t(20)=-2.6937; P=0.0139]

judge_notes: All three candidates agreed on the same three assays (OFT, EPM, MWM). No assays merged or dropped.

OFT D5_followup: candidates split (qwen=1, glm=0, gptoss=0). Adopted 0 — the OFT is a single session run 24 h post-dose; there is no second post-acute behavioural session for this assay (the 24 h delay is captured in time_to_assay, not as a separate follow-up recording).
EPM D5_followup: same reasoning as OFT — scored 0.
MWM D5_followup: scored 1 because behavioural recordings continue across D2-D7, all ≥24 h after the last drug dose, so post-acute follow-up data is collected.
B1 for OFT: only distance was measured → score 0 (1 measure). Glm's score of 1 was an error per rubric (1 measure = 0 points).

B1 for EPM: % open-arm entries, % open-arm time, closed-arm entries, risk-assessment time — 4 distinct measures could justify score 2, but the paper reports closed-arm entries only as a locomotor index and emphasizes the 3 anxiety measures. Adopted score 1 (2-3 measures) consistent with majority of candidates and conservative reading.
B1 for MWM: latency, time in quadrant, distance in quadrant, platform crossings = 4 measures → score 2.
MWM water_restriction: marked 'no' since the test medium is water; the animal is in water throughout, distinct from absence of drinking water.
Food/water_restriction for OFT/EPM set to 'during' (food/water not accessible in apparatus) per rubric default for short standard tests.
